notes.subject: car
notes.text: Only Generation 3 exists, all with a solid white car and no antenna.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short white plates with blue text; the blue can vanish in the blur.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Large red bricks and an unfinished look on many buildings, also common in parts of Peru.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Centre lines can be all yellow, yellow and white, or all white; edge lines are always white.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Concrete slab roads are fairly common, plus lots of cobblestone with neat lines of stones separating the messy ones.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bulky white square signposts, where Peru uses striped ones.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Yellow and black marked guardrails with the yellow stripes always on the outside.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Round concrete poles with pinholes, or wooden poles; extremely curvy wooden poles made of tree trunks are a strong clue in the east.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles are inconsistent; Argentine-style concrete poles occasionally appear.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black top with "Km" and white bottom with the distance; no road number.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Many women wear bowler hats, colourful shawls and big pleated skirts; also seen in nearby parts of Peru.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Objects painted black, white and a big blue field, with graffiti of the former ruling party and president.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A second official flag, a square patchwork of seven diagonal colours, often on government buildings.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Ads for a blue-logo telecom company that does not operate in neighbouring Peru.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rocks and soil often have a reddish tint, stronger than in the other Andean countries.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: A huge highland plateau of grass in the west, with tufted grass; the road is flat but hills surround it.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The plateau is greener in the north near the big twin cities and drier in the south around Oruro.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A very green landscape around the huge lake on the border, seen from Ruta 1 and Ruta 2.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat, green, tropical land with farms and pink soil east of the Andes, around Santa Cruz.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Cobblestone roads are mainly in and southeast of Cochabamba.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The twin cities are very hilly; the western one has green hills, eroded yellow-beige sandstone pillars and the only 10+ storey buildings.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: On a flat dusty plateau with grid streets, lots of semi-finished brick, and colourful Neo-Andean facades.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A flat valley with a wall of mountains to the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The driest landscape of the big cities, with a large dry hill to the west.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Arid hilly land with a huge bare pyramid mountain stripped by silver mining.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A lone snow-capped volcano seen from southwest Ruta 4 and in a national park.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: A bendy unpaved mountain road through tropical jungle hills, foggy in the south.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The only large divided highway runs between the twin cities and Oruro.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: A square smudge on the front left of the camera along Ruta 4 from the plateau east toward the lowlands.
